terms.meaning: A stack of cells where each cell is the sum of the two cells just below it.
1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13… where each number is the sum of the two before it.

items.name: Think of a number
items.formula: Call it x and follow each step
items.example: Double, add 6, halve, subtract x: 2x → 2x + 6 → x + 3 → 3. The answer is always 3.

items.name: Top of a 3-row pyramid
items.formula: Bottom a, b, c: top = a + 2b + c

items.name: Top of a 4-row pyramid
items.formula: Bottom a, b, c, d: top = a + 3b + 3c + d

items.name: 2 × 2 square on a calendar
items.formula: Dates a, a + 1, a + 7, a + 8: sum = 4a + 16

items.name: Largest product from three digits
items.formula: Use the largest digit alone, and the rest as the larger 2-digit number

items.name: Heads and legs
items.example: 10 heads and 28 legs: 2h + 4(10 − h) = 28, so 6 hens and 4 horses.

items.name: Working backwards
items.formula: Undo each step in reverse order
items.example: Double a number and subtract 4 to get 10. Add 4 to get 14, then halve: 7.

mistakes.text: A 2-digit number ab means 10a + b, not a × b or a + b.
In a 3-row pyramid the middle bottom number counts twice, because it feeds two cells above it.
When working backwards, undo the last step first. Subtracting after doubling is undone by adding before halving.
